title: Annotatio VI §.II Mode: Acerbic treatment — odious; prostitutes sacred order and the Protestant cause
pass_a_gloss: The Mode of treating is for the most part more acerbic, hated by all pious Christians whatever no less than by the more cordate Theologians themselves, and foully prostituting sacred things and the Sacred order and the Protestant Cause, and all but infaming them in the worst way — projected even below the quarrels, altercations, calumnies, contumelious words and shamelessnesses of the vulgar and of old women themselves —
pass_b_english: The mode of treatment is usually more acerbic.
Pious Christians and the more sober theologians alike hate it.

It foully prostitutes sacred things, the sacred order, and the Protestant cause — and nearly brands them with the worst infamy — sunk even below the quarrels, calumnies, and shameless abuse of the crowd and of old women.
source_text: Modum tractandi plerumque acerbiorem, omnibusque tàm piis Christianis quibuscunque, quàm ipsis Theologis cordatioribus exosum, ac res sacras, & Sacrum ordinem, & Causam Protestanticam, turpiter prostituentem, & tantum non pessimum in modum infamantem, etiam vel infra vulgi ipsarumque vetularum rixas, altercationes, calumnias, verba contumeliosa atque propudia projectum,
